text: Yaskawa's ROS 2 driver, which runs on the robot controller as a MotoPlus application and connects to ROS 2 through a micro-ROS Agent on the PC.
The premier open-source motion planning framework for ROS 2, providing 3D collision checking, inverse kinematics, and trajectory execution.
A MoveIt 2 library (MTC) that breaks a manipulation job such as pick and place into a chain of stages that are planned together and can be inspected one by one in RViz.
A joint move, in which all joints move together to reach a target, so the tool usually does not travel in a straight line; it is written MoveJ in ABB RAPID.
A robot motion command that moves the arm to target coordinates in joint space, causing all axes to arrive simultaneously along curved paths.
A linear move, in which the tool center point travels in a straight line to its target; it is written MoveL in ABB RAPID.
One step of a MoveIt Task Constructor task, such as moving to a named pose, generating grasp poses or attaching an object, which produces or connects robot states.
A name prefix, such as /turtlesim1, added to a node's name and its relative topic names so that identical nodes can run side by side without conflicts.
A single program in ROS that performs one specific job, such as reading a sensor or planning a path, and communicates with other nodes.
Unpredictable odometry errors caused by external floor interactions, such as wheel slip, floor bumps, or skidding during turns, which vary randomly between runs.
Controlling a machine tool's motion with numbers stored on a medium, developed for machine tools in the 1950s and a bridge between punched cards and robot programs.
A world-fixed frame in which the robot's pose changes smoothly but slowly drifts.
The use of data from motion sensors (such as wheel encoders) to estimate a mobile robot's change in position and heading over time relative to a starting pose.
Writing and testing a robot program on a computer in 3D simulation, so the real robot can keep working until the finished program is downloaded to it.
A RAPID function that returns a copy of a robtarget moved by given X, Y and Z distances in millimeters, in the work object's coordinate system.
Open Navigation LLC, the company that provides leadership, maintenance, development and support services for Nav2.
An alliance formed under the Open Source Robotics Foundation in 2024 to guide and support the ongoing development of ROS, Gazebo, and Open-RMF.
An automatic thresholding method that determines an optimal global cutoff by minimizing intra-class intensity variance on bimodal histograms.
The XML manifest file in a ROS package that lists the package name, description, maintainer, software license, and the dependencies needed to build and run it.
A RAPID persistent variable that remembers the last value it was assigned even if the program is stopped and started from the beginning, used for taught points, tool data and cycle counters.
A feedback control loop that calculates corrective motor commands by combining current error, accumulated past error, and the error's rate of change to hold a target speed or position.
An exchange of latched request and acknowledge signals (such as cycle-start, busy and done) between a PLC and a robot so each knows the other's state.
A URScript function that combines two poses, used to convert a pose given in a feature or tool frame into the base frame, for example to compute an approach point.
The time-update phase of a Kalman filter where the previous state and covariance are projected forward in time using a physical process model.
The uncertainty in a robot's motion prediction caused by real-world physical disturbances such as wheel slip and uneven terrain, represented by matrix Q in a Kalman filter.
A visual outline in Universal Robots PolyScope that displays robot commands, waypoints, and logic as an expandable list of steps instead of written text code.
A sensor that measures the internal physical state of a robot, such as motor speed, joint angle, wheel rotation, or internal battery temperature.
A file in a repository that pre-fills every new pull request with prompts and a checklist, so contributors give reviewers the information they need.
An off-delay circuit in a high-speed sensor ensuring fast signals persist long enough for slower PLC scan cycles to detect them.
A digital signaling method that simulates variable analog power levels by switching a square wave between HIGH and LOW at a rapid frequency.
A readable, high-level programming language widely used in robotics for scripting, testing and higher-level logic, and one of the two main languages used with ROS.
An encoder arrangement with two channels offset by a quarter cycle, so the order in which they change shows the direction of rotation.
A signal processing technique that decodes two 90-degree phase-shifted channels (A and B) to determine both rotational velocity and directional polarity.
A RAPID instruction that raises an error, or, used bare inside an error handler, passes the current error on to the calling routine's handler.

Random Sample Consensus, an algorithm that finds geometric shapes (such as flat tables) in noisy point clouds by repeatedly testing random sample points against a distance threshold to ignore outliers.
A named block of ABB RAPID code, from MODULE to ENDMODULE, that holds data declarations at the top followed by routines such as PROC, FUNC and TRAP.
The official Python client library for ROS 2, providing classes for nodes, publishers, subscribers, timers, and service servers.
The average distance in pixels between where known pattern points are detected in images and where the calibration predicts they should appear; lower is better.
The introductory file in an open-source repository that explains what the project does, why it is useful, and how to install and run the code.
A Linux kernel built or tuned (for example PREEMPT_RT or low-latency) so that time-critical tasks such as a 500 Hz robot control loop meet their deadlines.
A gearbox in a robot joint that lowers the motor's speed and raises its torque, such as an RV or strain-wave (harmonic) gear.
The economic process where new technology creates entirely new jobs and complex tasks for people, such as programming, integrating, and maintaining industrial robot cells.
An ABB RAPID function that shifts a target along the axes of the tool, often used to compute approach and retract points from a grip point.
How closely a robot returns to the same programmed point again and again, given on spec sheets in millimeters, for example ±0.02 mm.
ROS Middleware, an abstraction layer that connects high-level ROS 2 client libraries to underlying communication systems such as DDS or Zenoh without changing user code.
A machine that senses its surroundings, decides what to do with a program, and acts on the world, such as a six-axis arm guided by a program on an assembly line.
The number of operating industrial robots for every 10,000 factory workers. The International Federation of Robotics uses this measure to compare how automated different countries are.
A widely deployed ROS 2 package providing non-linear state estimation through continuous, multi-sensor fused Extended and Unscented Kalman Filters.
ABB's 3D offline programming and simulation suite that runs a binary Virtual Controller to achieve exact path and cycle-time parity with physical robots.
An ABB RAPID data type that defines a complete robot position in millimeters, tool orientation as a quaternion, arm axis configurations, and external axis positions.
Robot Operating System, an open-source middleware framework providing libraries, tools, and message-passing protocols for building robot applications.
The ROS 1 command that starts the central master every node registers with, along with the global parameter server; ROS 2 has no such central server.
The command-line dependency management tool that inspects a ROS package's package.xml and installs missing system libraries via the host OS package manager.
A way to represent 3D orientation where the vector's direction points along the axis of rotation and its length gives the rotation angle in radians, used in URScript poses.
A seven-segment motion plan that also limits jerk, so acceleration ramps up and down gradually and the speed curve has rounded S-shaped corners.
The fixed interval at which a digital controller reads its sensor and updates its output, such as 100 ms in the Arduino PID Library by default.
Selective Compliance Assembly Robot Arm: a fast, compact, usually four-axis arm that swings in a horizontal plane and is stiff vertically, widely used for pick-and-place and small-part assembly.
A device that measures the robot or its surroundings, such as an encoder, an ultrasonic range finder or a camera; it is the "sense" part of the sense, think, act loop.
The process of combining data from multiple different sensors so the resulting estimate of a robot's position or movement has less uncertainty than any single sensor alone.
A two-way communication pattern in ROS where a client node sends a request to a server node and waits for a response, used for quick one-off tasks.
A robot that performs useful tasks for people or equipment outside industrial factory work, such as cleaning, delivery, inspection, or hospitality.
A control protocol for RC hobby servos where shaft angular position is proportional to a positive pulse width (1.0 ms to 2.0 ms) repeated every 20 ms (50 Hz).
A small configuration file in a Python ROS 2 package that installs its executables into lib/<package> so that ros2 run can find them.
The key that apt uses to check that packages from a software repository are genuine; the ROS apt source package installs it together with the repository configuration.
The difference between a simulated robot in software and its real physical motion, caused by part tolerances, slight fixture misalignments, and mechanical arm deflection.
A robot pose where a small tool motion can demand very fast joint motion, such as a fully stretched arm or aligned wrist axes.
A DC circuit configuration providing a path to supply common (-).
Simultaneous Localization and Mapping, the method a mobile robot uses to build a map of an unknown room while tracking its own location inside it.
A DC circuit configuration providing a path to supply source (+).
A robot wrist whose last three joint axes meet at one point, which lets inverse kinematics split into a position part and an orientation part.
A program that is always in exactly one of a fixed set of states and moves to another state when a given event happens (also called a finite state machine).
Pulsing an LED light in brief, intense flashes timed with camera exposure. This reduces heat, extends LED life, and freezes the motion of fast-moving parts on conveyors.
A placeholder in a ROS 2 launch file (such as LaunchConfiguration or FindPackageShare) whose actual value is determined only when the launch file runs.
Rodney Brooks's 1986 reactive control design, in which simple behaviors are stacked in layers and higher layers can suppress the outputs of lower ones while the lower layers keep running.

Consistent odometry errors caused by physical robot imperfections, such as unequal wheel diameters or wheelbase uncertainty, that repeat identically across runs and can be corrected by software calibration.
A specialized optical lens whose chief rays run parallel to the optical axis, maintaining constant image size and eliminating perspective error even as object distance changes.
Controlling a robot remotely in real time, as a surgeon does with the da Vinci system, so the robot follows a human operator rather than acting on its own.
A computer vision technique that slides a small reference template image across a larger search image to find the position of highest visual correlation.
A platform support level in ROS 2 (defined in REP 2000) that receives automated continuous integration testing, binary Debian/zip releases, and official bug fixes.
The step, done in MoveIt after path planning, that adds timestamps, velocities and accelerations to a list of waypoints while respecting the robot's limits.
A function s(t) that runs from 0 to 1 over a move and says what fraction of the path the robot should have covered at each moment.
A distance measurement technique that calculates distance by measuring the precise elapsed time required for emitted acoustic or optical photons to return from a target.
The 16-bit internal hardware timer/counter peripheral on the ATmega328P responsible for generating PWM on pins 9 and 10 and serving the Arduino Servo library.

The working point of the tool, such as the tip of a welding wire or the center between gripper fingers, which the robot positions and moves; on ABB robots the default tool0 has its TCP at the mounting flange.
The digital and analog inputs and outputs, plus switchable power, at a robot's wrist connector, used to drive and sense a gripper without cables along the arm.
The RAPID data type that describes a tool: whether the robot holds it, its TCP frame, and its load (mass, center of gravity and inertia).
A motion plan in which an axis speeds up at constant acceleration, cruises at its maximum speed, then slows down at the same rate, so its speed-time graph is a trapezoid.
The shape a trapezoidal profile takes on a move too short to reach maximum speed: the axis speeds up and then immediately slows down, with no cruise phase.
A tiny 2D ROS simulator of a turtle that uses the same nodes, topics and services as a real robot, made for learning ROS.
The Long Term Support (LTS) release of Canonical Ubuntu Linux serving as the primary reference Tier 1 target for ROS 2 Lyrical Luth.
User Datagram Protocol, a lighter and faster network protocol than TCP that does not guarantee delivery, and the transport DDS uses in ROS 2.
The University of Michigan Benchmark, a calibration test where a robot drives clockwise and counter-clockwise square paths to separate and measure wheel diameter differences and wheelbase errors.
The existing base ROS 2 installation or workspace (such as /opt/ros/lyrical) that an overlay workspace builds upon and relies on for dependencies.
The first industrial robot, developed by George Devol and Joseph Engelberger, which began handling hot die-cast parts at a General Motors plant in New Jersey in 1961.
Unified Robot Description Format: an XML file that describes a robot as a tree of links joined by joints, with each joint's type, axis, position and limits.
Universal Robots' free simulator that runs the PolyScope teach-pendant software and a simulated controller on a computer, for example in a Docker container.
Using a camera and vision software to find where a part is, so the robot program can adjust its taught points to the part's actual position.
A coordinate frame attached to a fixture or workpiece that program targets are measured from, so re-teaching it moves all targets without changing the program.
Windows Subsystem for Linux version 2, a Windows tool that runs a real Linux kernel, allowing developers to install Ubuntu and run ROS tools directly on Windows.
A lightweight communication protocol supported as an alternative middleware in ROS 2, designed with low network overhead for mobile robots and challenging wireless links.
A classic PID tuning method that finds the gain at which the system oscillates steadily (Ku) and its period (Pu), then calculates starting values for Kp, Ki and Kd.
